newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses weaken in bout of profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses weaken in bout of profit-taking.

text.p: European bourses eased back on Wednesday from recent record levels as a mixed overnight session on Wall Street encouraged a bout of profit-taking.

On currency markets, the dollar strengthened with speculation growing about an increase in U.S. interest rates and dealers awaiting the release of the American central bank's Beige Book assessment of the state of the country's economy.
The disappointing showing on equity markets followed an unsettled day on Tuesday when European shares backtracked after roaring to new record trading highs in early business.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, was hurt the least by the downturn in European sentiment. The FTSE index had slipped only 0.2 percent by lunchtime after closing at new peaks for the previous six sessions.
"The market is looking a bit weary this morning," the head of sales and trading at a major investment bank said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see a few down days."

"Wall Street didn't do much so there is no reason to rush in and start buying. The Dow is probably going to head lower today so that will encourage a bit of profit-taking here," one trader said. On Tuesday, the Dow closed 5.77 points up at a new peak of 7,085.16.
Though the Dow edged to a record, the overall market was nervous because of speculation that the Federal Reserve might be planning an interest rate increase.
Investors were worried about Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings recently that stocks could be overvalued and that the central bank might raise short-term interest rates.
In Paris, stocks fell 0.9 in thin volumes, depressed by worries about long-term interest rate trends that fuelled profit-taking, traders said.

"A lot of analysts are unclear where the market's going from here," said Olivier Blitz at IFF Bourse. The bourse's underlying upward trend looked intact, particularly if the futures contract held above 2,670 points. If it broke that level, he said, a significant correction might take place.

Against the trend, shares in Lafarge rose 1.63 percent to 373.50 francs at one point after the group reported net attributable profit of 1.85 billion francs ($321 million), which was well received by the market.
In Frankfurt, German shares weakened as chemicals group Hoechst AG fell 3.25 marks, more than four percent, to 71.95 after it shelved plans to list its HMR Marion Roussel unit.
"But apart from that, it's relatively steady, although what is worrying at the moment is that there are no impulses to be seen on the upside," said one dealer.
In currencies, the dollar was up by nearly a yen and half a pfennig at midday on the strength of speculation about higher U.S. interest rates as dealers awaited the Beige Book report at 1900 GMT.

Talk that the central bank might increase rates at its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25 has ebbed and flowed since the release of February U.S. employment data on Friday.
While brisk job growth is still evident, it has not yet been mirrored by any signs of wage inflation, analysts said.

"The market's getting a little nervous about this month's FOMC and that should continue to prove dollar supportive as speculation about a rate rise circulates," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7083 marks and 122.79 yen compared with 1.7038 marks and 121.82 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 8.6 points at 4,435.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 24.06 points at 2,662.09.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 48.81 points at 3,411.78.
PRECIOUS METALS 1215 GMT
Gold was fixed at $353.15 an ounce compared to $351.40 at the close on Tuesday. Silver was at $5.24, up three cents. ($ = 5.760 French Francs)
